newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: UOB sees Malaysian unit merger in June.
newsitem.headline: UOB sees Malaysian unit merger in June.

text.p: Singapore's United Overseas Bank Ltd said on Thursday it expected its Malaysian subsidiaries, Chung Khiaw Bank (Malaysia) Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd, to complete their merger in June.

"In principle, Bank Negara has approved our proposal for the banks to merge. It is proceeding. Hopefully by June we will merge as one bank in Malaysia," UOB chairman and chief executive officer Wee Cho Yaw told reporters.
Wee was speaking after the bank released its 1996 financial results showing a 13.1 percent rise in net profit to Singapore $715.52 million.
Wee said UOB's Malaysian operations expanded 30 percent in 1996 and made a net profit of Singapore $131 million.
"The Malaysian economy is still very strong, particularly on the manufacturing side. I still believe Malaysia has a lot of potential and the growth in Malaysia will continue," he said.
Asked by reporters whether the recent diplomatic spat between Singapore and Malaysia would hurt the bank's operations, Wee said he left politics to the politicians and didn't want to get involved.
